validity.recommendation: Existence of a distinct 'El Wasta–Beni Suef' 65 km reinforcement line is corroborated (World Bank ESIA item #3 of 9 + egy-map.com government project tracker) and should stay in the tracker – but swap the Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start/Diameter citation off petro-news.com/95212, which on close read is actually about the ADJACENT/SIBLING 'Dahshour–El Wasta' pipeline, not this one. Also verify the Owner field (EGAS holding co vs. GASCO the documented implementer/operator) and flag the unresolved 61 km vs 65 km length discrepancy for a human check.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: The sheet's own cited source (petro-news.com/95212, an Arabic listicle of 39 Sisi-era petroleum projects) was fetched and read in full. It contains exactly ONE mention of 'الواسطى' (El Wasta): item #14, 'تدشين خط غاز دهشور – الواسطى' = 'Inauguration of the Dahshour–El Wasta gas line,' purpose 'feed Beni Suef power station and the Upper Egypt region,' 36-inch diameter, 65 km, cost 525,000,000 EGP. There is NO separate mention on that page of an 'El Wasta–Beni Suef' line – the citation currently attached to this row is for the NEIGHBORING segment, not this one (confirmed by grepping the raw page text for the Arabic string; only one hit, tied to the Dahshour–Wasta name). This matches url_verifier's own flag that the Status value 'operating' isn't textually present on that page.

Independent confirmation that 'El Wasta–Beni Suef' is nonetheless a real, DISTINCT project (not just a mislabel of Dahshour–El Wasta): (1) World Bank ESIA for the EG-Giza North Power Project savings package (SFG1795, Dec 2016) explicitly lists 9 GASCO pipelines funded from the same pot, with item #1 'New Capital–Dahshour (70 km)' [=GEM P3930, exact length match], item #2 'Dahshour–El Wasta gas pipeline (65 km)' [fully detailed elsewhere in the same doc: 36in, API 5L X60, 70 bar, 20.7 MMSCMD – this is the pipeline petro-news's article #14 is actually about], and item #3 'El Wasta–BeniSuef gas pipeline (65 km) + gas decompression station (in BeniSuef Power Station)' – a separate line item. (2) egy-map.com (Egyptian government infrastructure-achievements tracker, independent of GASCO/WB) has a page titled 'المرحلة الأولي لخط تدعيم الواسطي - بني سويف' ('Phase 1 of the El Wasta–Beni Suef reinforcement line'): 65 km, 36in, cost 555,000,000 EGP, completed Nov 2019, purpose = feed Beni Suef power station – which matches GEM's exact numbers (65.00 km / 36.00 in / 555,000,000 EGP) far more closely than petro-news's Dahshour–Wasta numbers (65 km/36in/525,000,000 EGP for the sibling line). This strongly suggests GEM's VALUES were sourced from something like egy-map.com, but the URL that ended up in the ref column is for the wrong sibling pipeline.

Oddity flagged, not resolved: the World Bank's own RAP document for this package (SFG1801, running header literally says 'RAP study for EG-GIZA North Power Project – El Wasta – Beni Suef Pipeline') describes a route that is verbatim identical to the Dahshour–El Wasta ESIA's route text ('starts at the pressure compression station in Dahshour...up to a distance of 8 km...continues...up to a distance of 57 km till it reaches an existing valve room on the Dahshour–Koraymt gas pipe line...total length of 65 km') – i.e. even the World Bank's paired ESIA/RAP filings appear to have cross-contaminated boilerplate between the two adjacent segments. This is a known-messy documentation cluster; it does not by itself disprove El Wasta–Beni Suef's existence (the ESIA's summary list is unambiguous that it's a separate 65 km line + Beni Suef decompression station), but it means no source I found gives a route or diameter that is unambiguously and exclusively about El Wasta–Beni Suef rather than reused Dahshour–El Wasta text.

Secondary lead, NOT verified (excluded from proposed_refs): search snippets attributed to GASCO's own pipelines page (gasco.com.eg/?page_id=5242) describe 'El-Wasta/Beni-Suef Gas pipeline (61 km – 36")...scheduled operation May 2019...capacity 22 MMSCMD for the 2 phases (El-Wasta/Beni-Suef and Dahshour/El Wasta pipelines)' – note '61 km' not '65 km'. I could not fetch gasco.com.eg directly (TLS cert error / unreachable) or find an archived copy, so I can't confirm this wording or cite it, but it's a second length figure (61 vs 65 km) worth a human check against GASCO's own records; capacity 22 MMSCMD for the combined two-phase project (not this segment alone) also should NOT be entered as this row's Capacity if pursued later.

CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk feeding a thermal power plant, not a gathering/plant-internal line – confirmed by all sources (WB, egy-map). Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission stand, just need a re-cited ref.

OWNER: sheet lists Owner1 = 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (100%) with no ref. Both World Bank documents state the 9-pipeline package including this line 'will be implemented by GASCO' (Egyptian Natural Gas Company, EGAS's transmission-operator subsidiary), not EGAS/Natural Gas Holding Co directly. EGAS-as-Owner (state holding parent) vs GASCO-as-Operator is a defensible split (common GEM convention), but flagging so Baird can confirm the sheet's Operator field (if any) carries GASCO rather than leaving Owner=EGAS unqualified.

DUPLICATE check against the 30-pipeline Egypt-operating roster and the GulfPub list: no roster row is named/specced as 'Dahshour–El Wasta' (the WB's item #2), so that sibling segment appears to be a genuine gap in GEM's roster (a Discovery-side matter, not a P3929 duplicate) rather than P3929 itself duplicating another PID. P3929's own specs (65km/36in, El Wasta→Beni Suef governorate) don't match South Valley Gas Pipeline segments P6698 (Al Kurimat→Beni Suef, 30km/32in) or P0477/P6697 closely enough to be the same physical pipe. GulfPub's Egypt gas roster has no El Wasta or Dahshour–El Wasta entry either.

fills.researcher_notes: Two source TYPES (Egyptian government project tracker egy-map.com, and the World Bank's official 9-pipeline funding list SFG1795) both give 65 km for 'El Wasta–BeniSuef gas pipeline' specifically – kept at tier=medium rather than high because both plausibly trace back to the same underlying GASCO/government announcement, and because an unverified GASCO-attributed search snippet gives 61 km instead (see validity notes) – flagging that discrepancy for a human check rather than asserting 65 km with full confidence.

egy-map.com gives an exact match to the sheet's existing value (555,000,000 EGP, 'بتكلفة 555 مليون جنيه'). Single source only for this exact figure (the sibling Dahshour–El Wasta line cost 525,000,000 EGP per petro-news, confirming these are two different budget lines rather than the same number restated) – tier=medium, single strong source, no second independent source found for the cost specifically.

Start=El Wasta (Beni Suef governorate town) and End=Beni Suef governorate/Beni Suef power station both corroborated by egy-map.com (purpose: feed Beni Suef power station) and the World Bank's 9-pipeline list item #3 ('El Wasta–BeniSuef gas pipeline...decompression station in BeniSuef Power Station'). No source gives a more granular end location than 'Beni Suef Power Station' (Ghayadah/Biba area) – left EndLocation blank rather than guessing.

routes.start_name: El Wasta, Beni Suef Governorate, Egypt
routes.end_name: Beni Suef Thermal Power Plant (Ghayadah, near Biba, Beni Suef Governorate)
routes.corridor_desc: Loosely bounded only. Named endpoints are reasonably solid: El Wasta town (start, per egy-map.com and the WB 9-pipeline list) and the Beni Suef thermal power plant / decompression station, located near the village of Ghayadah east of Biba town center, Beni Suef Governorate (end, per egy-map.com purpose statement and WB ESIA item #3). El Wasta and Biba/Ghayadah are only ~45-50 km apart on a direct Nile-valley line, well short of the pipeline's stated 65 km, so the true corridor must deviate – most plausibly it continues the pattern documented for the adjacent, well-sourced Dahshour–El Wasta segment (which runs on the DESERT side, west of the Nile, paralleling the Cairo–Fayoum road then the Western Cairo–Asyut desert road, rather than through the populated floodplain) south from El Wasta to a decompression station within the Beni Suef power-plant complex. I could not find a source describing THIS segment's specific route (as opposed to the sibling segment's), so this is an inferred extension of a documented pattern, not a sourced path – no waypoints are asserted, and end coordinates are the nearest town (Biba) rather than the plant itself, since I could not independently source the plant's precise coordinates (a GEM wiki page exists for 'Beni Suef power plant' but per standing rules GEM cannot be cited/used as the coordinate source).
routes.researcher_notes: start_lat/lon for El Wasta town and end_lat/lon for Biba town (nearest named place to the Beni Suef power plant/decompression station) sourced from db-city.com gazetteer coordinates (non-GEM, independent of the pipeline sources); NOT the plant's own coordinates, which I could not independently confirm outside of GEM's own wiki page (excluded per standing rules). No coordinates fabricated – no waypoints given since no source describes the actual routed path for this specific segment (only the sibling Dahshour–El Wasta segment's route is documented).

summary: El Wasta–Beni Suef Gas Pipeline is very likely real (WB's 9-pipeline funding list + egy-map.com both name it as a distinct 65 km line feeding Beni Suef power station), but the sheet's current citation (petro-news.com/95212) is actually about the adjacent Dahshour–El Wasta sibling pipeline, not this one — flagged as attribution concern; re-cited Length/Location/SegmentCost to egy-map.com + WB doc (medium/high tier); route given as loose corridor only (suggested accuracy stays low); a 61km-vs-65km length discrepancy (unverified GASCO snippet) and Owner=EGAS-vs-GASCO-as-operator are left as open human checks.
